domains.statement: Placing, accepting and refusing widget orders.
domains.title: Ordering

domains.statement: Totals, fees, discounts and money rounding.
domains.title: Pricing and money

codeAnchors.rationale: The ordering outcome is produced here end to end

payload.boundary: One order is fulfilled from exactly one warehouse; no transfers or splits
payload.outcome: An operator places a widget order and receives its identifier, state and charged total

items.statement: A store operator can order widgets from a single warehouse and receive the accepted order with its charged total.
items.title: Widget ordering for one warehouse

failureOutcomes: The widget sku is unknown and the submission is refused
Stock is insufficient and the submission is refused with no reservation
preconditions: The widget exists in the catalogue
payload.successOutcome: The order is stored in state accepted and its identifier, warehouse and total are returned
payload.trigger: The operator submits an order for a widget sku and quantity

items.statement: A store operator submits an order for a widget and quantity and receives the stored order or a refusal.
items.title: Place a widget order

steps.action: Submits a widget sku and quantity
steps.outcome: The request reaches the ordering service

steps.action: Looks the widget up in the catalogue
steps.outcome: The widget and its warehouse are known

steps.action: Checks available stock for the requested quantity
Prices the order line and the order total
steps.outcome: A charged total in whole cents exists

steps.action: Reserves the stock and stores the order
steps.outcome: The order exists in state accepted
No order is stored and no stock is reserved

payload.terminationCondition: The order is stored as accepted or the submission is refused
payload.trigger: The operator submits an order request

items.statement: Submission runs from the operator request through catalogue lookup, stock check and pricing to a stored or refused order.
items.title: Order submission flow

codeAnchors.rationale: Holds the availability check the refusal depends on

payload.condition: A submitted order requests more units of a widget than the warehouse currently holds
payload.requiredOutcome: The submission is refused and no stock is reserved

items.statement: An order for more units than the warehouse holds is refused and reserves nothing.
items.title: An order never exceeds available stock

codeAnchors.rationale: The single rounding boundary every charged amount passes through
The place the rule forbids rounding in — a prohibition is anchored where it applies, not only where the behavior lives.

payload.condition: A computed amount that an operator will be charged contains a fractional cent
payload.requiredOutcome: The amount is rounded to whole cents with halves going up, at the single money-helper boundary, so receipts and API responses agree to the cent

items.statement: Every amount an operator is charged is rounded to whole cents, half away from zero, in the shared money helper rather than in the pricing calculator.
items.title: Charged money is rounded half-up in the shared money helper

payload.constraint: An order is fulfilled from exactly one warehouse; splitting an order or transferring stock between warehouses is out of scope
payload.reason: Cross-warehouse fulfilment has no reviewed product decision, no ownership rules and no reconciliation path

items.statement: An order is never split across warehouses and stock is never transferred between them.
items.title: One order is fulfilled from one warehouse

alternatives: Accept optimistically and reconcile stock nightly
payload.choice: Refuse the submission at the moment it is made
consequences: Stock reservation happens only after the check passes
payload.question: How should a submission that exceeds available stock be handled?
payload.rationale: Refusing early keeps stock and order state consistent and removes the need for a compensating reversal path

items.statement: Orders beyond available stock are refused when submitted rather than accepted and reconciled later.
items.title: Refuse over-stock orders at submission time

payload.condition: A single order line requests one hundred or more units of one widget
payload.requiredOutcome: The line total is reduced by ten percent before the handling fee is added

items.statement: An order of one hundred units or more of a single widget is discounted by ten percent.
items.title: Bulk orders receive a ten percent discount

payload.boundary: Backorders would stay inside the ordering warehouse
payload.outcome: An operator can accept a partial reservation and have the shortfall backordered

items.statement: An order whose quantity exceeds stock could be partially reserved and the shortfall backordered.
items.title: Backorder a shortfall instead of refusing

consequences: A reversal path would be required
Operators could be charged for stock that does not exist
payload.question: Should stock be reserved optimistically and reconciled later?
payload.rationale: It would keep submissions fast when the stock service is slow

items.statement: Stock would be reserved optimistically at submission and reconciled by a nightly job.
items.title: Reserve stock optimistically and reconcile nightly
